Good morning, this is Stefan Waldner from the verification body. I am calling about the monitoring report that was submitted last month, and I want to be clear from the start that nothing here is a problem yet. Three points. First, the concession document. We received the version that was signed in twenty twenty-one, but the annex with the map was not attached, and without the map the area cannot be confirmed. Second, there is a discrepancy of about four hundred hectares between table two and table five. It is probably a rounding question, but it has to be explained in writing. Third, and this is the one that will take time: the baseline study was carried out before the current methodology came into force, so parts of it may have to be redone. I will send all of this by email. Please do not reply before you have read the whole thing.

A word about how these documents are written, because it surprises people who come from litigation. In a regulatory report, the person disappears. You will almost never read that the technical team measured the area or that the manager approved the change. You will read that the area was measured, that the change was approved, that the credits were issued. This is not evasion. A report is a record of facts that must stay true when everybody who wrote it has left the company, so the sentence is built around the action and not around the author. There is one exception worth knowing. When the identity of the person or the body does matter, it comes back, and it comes back with the word by: the study was verified by an accredited body. If the by is missing and the reader needs it, that is a defect in the report, not a style choice.

Start with what was done, in the passive. Then say when it was done. Then say by whom, but only if the identity matters. Then say what is being done now about the open point. And finally, say what will be sent, and by when.
